Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan & benchmark criteria (Acme Corp)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is the draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) section for the technical evaluation milestone — I pulled together the benchmark success criteria and an initial model shortlist based on what we discussed. High level:

- Target close date for the MAP milestone: 2026-12-15
- Success criteria: p50 latency under 150ms for standard 512-token requests; p99 under 350ms; semantic similarity >= 0.78 on your intent set; cost target under $0.20 per 1k tokens for inference (post-quantization estimate)
- Model shortlist: Llama-3-16B (quantized), Mistral-Instruct, Redmond-Base-7B (opt) — we recommend starting with Llama-3 and Mistral for coverage
- Responsibilities: Redwood SE (Dev Patel) to run benchmarks and provide logs; Acme SRE to validate network egress and run sample traffic; Procurement to confirm security/contract items (Rishi is in copy for any negotiation needs)
- Dependencies: access to a 24-hour sample of production-ish traffic, a subset of labeled intents for the semantic similarity test, and estimated SLOs for peak QPS

Please review and confirm whether the targets look reasonable for your team. If fine, we'll lock the MAP milestone and Dev will kick off the benchmark next week.

Attachments: ACME_MAP_DRAFT_v2.pdf; acme-benchmarks-template.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- The latency targets look reasonable, but we need to make sure we can reproduce p99 under peak traffic (our peak QPS spikes ~3x baseline during checkout). Can we capture a 2-hour peak window?
- For the semantic similarity test, Priya will send the labeled intent set (approx 1.2k examples) by end of day Monday.
- One addition to the MAP: can we add a short security validation milestone (SaaS data flow diagram + SOC2 evidence request) as a dependency? Procurement will need that before signing.

If those are included, we can commit to the 2026-12-15 internal target. Also fine with starting with Llama-3 + Mistral.

Thanks —

Alex —

Great, thanks for the quick review and for flagging the security milestone. I updated the MAP draft and the benchmarks template to include:

- Security validation milestone: Redwood to provide SOC2 summary + data flow diagram within 3 business days of MAP lock; Acme to provide any specific compliance controls checklist.
- Peak window: we'll capture a 2-hour peak window as you requested — please confirm the expected timezone for the window and an ETA for the sample traffic export.

I've assigned Dev Patel as the SE lead for the benchmark execution (copied). Dev — can you take ownership of the benchmark runs and share a test matrix + schedule by Monday? Plan is: baseline model latency/cost runs, semantic similarity eval on Acme intent set, end-to-end throughput test using the peak window, and a short regression check for hallucination rate on a 200-example safety set.

Next steps for Acme: confirm sample traffic window and share intent set (Priya), confirm who on procurement will own the security checklist so we can route evidence. After we get those, Dev will provide a timeline and we can lock the MAP milestone date (2026-12-15).

Marissa

Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan & benchmark criteria (Acme Corp)

Thanks Marissa / Alex —

I'll take point on the technical evaluation. Quick plan and asks:

1) Test matrix (initial):
   - Models: Llama-3-16B (q4_0), Mistral-Instruct (base), Redmond-Base-7B (int8)
   - Workloads: 512-token generation (avg request), 128-token short responses (chat), batch inference (qps=baseline and peak)
   - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens (est.), semantic similarity (cosine) vs. Acme labels, hallucination/regression rate

2) Targets we'll attempt to validate based on your MAP:
   - p50 latency < 150ms (512 tokens)
   - p99 latency < 350ms (512 tokens)
   - Cost < $0.20 per 1k tokens (after quantization & batching)
   - Semantic similarity >= 0.78 on provided intent set

3) Asks from Acme:
   - Sample traffic export (2-hour peak window) in ndjson (timestamp, request_text, session_id) or a shared replayable load; ETA?
   - Labeled intent set (Priya)
   - A contact in procurement for the security checklist (SOC2 artifacts)

I will prepare the detailed test matrix and a runnable benchmark script by Monday EOD and share the run schedule. If Acme can provide the traffic and labels early next week we can complete the run and deliver results by 2026-12-06, leaving time for follow-up.

Attachments referenced: acme-benchmarks-template.xlsx (I'll populate the test rows before the run)

Cheers,
